overall: Atlanta is experiencing a warming but moderating Tuesday morning, with temperatures reaching 80.6°F by 11:50 ET under a mix of scattered clouds (62% cloud fraction) and a brisk NW wind near 14 mph with gusts to 25 mph. The temperature is still rising at +1.8°F/hr but decelerating sharply (acceleration = -2.7°F/hr²), suggesting the warming pace will taper off before the afternoon peak. Conditions are cooler and windier than a typical June setup, consistent with a post-frontal airmass; the flood warnings in far SE Georgia are river-based and not directly relevant to Atlanta's temperature today.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP model agreement is unusually tight — ECMWF (82.3°F), HRRR (82.7°F), and NBM (82.6°F) are all within 0.4°F of each other and align closely with the NWS narrative high of 'near 83°F.' However, the intraday observation-driven model leans higher, with the peak timing estimated around 14.2h ET (roughly 2:10 PM), and the META fused model places the most probability on the 84–85°F bucket (32.2%), suggesting current surface heating dynamics may carry temps slightly above the NWP consensus.
max_temp_prediction: With 80.6°F already in hand at 11:50 ET and the peak still roughly 2+ hours away, a final high in the low-to-mid 80s is well-supported. The tight NWP cluster at 82–83°F provides a strong anchor, but the continuing positive velocity and the intraday/META models both tilting toward 84–85°F suggest a modest upside bias; 83–84°F is the most likely landing zone. Confidence is moderately high given excellent model agreement, though the decelerating warming rate and 62% cloud cover introduce some cap on the upper end.
